title: Spike-count variability ranks agree across gratings and scenes in 32 selected Allen mice
abstract: We tested whether neuron variability ranks agree between static gratings and natural scenes within the same mouse and brain area. We used public Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels summary tables. In 6,049 selected visual cortical neurons from 32 mice, the mean within-area partial rank correlation was 0.661, with a 95% mouse-bootstrap interval of 0.635 to 0.688. Controls included both stimulus block rates, waveform duration and four recording-quality measures. All 32 mouse scores were positive. Stricter quality and rate filters kept the positive association. No paired source values were equal within 1e-10. This is a benchmark for transfer of a functional summary across two stimuli. It does not show a wiring mechanism, an intrinsic cell property, or transfer across species. Preferred-condition count means and trial-level uncertainty were not measured. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions. External record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Within-area variability rank agreement across two stimulus blocks. Points are mean Fisher-transformed correlations, converted back. Bars are pointwise 95% mouse-bootstrap intervals. Blue areas are visual cortex. Brown areas are exploratory extensions.

citations.reason: Stimulus-dependent regional quenching motivates a distinct within-area, same-neuron transfer test. No code or table reused.
Regional reliability motivates testing transfer at the neuron level without a wiring claim.
